book: The First Epistle of Clement to the Corinthians
status: drafted via lean single-pass workflow grounded in the real extracted verse text
notes: Source file read in full (E:/Unity/Clicker_Genesis/Assets/Resources/Verses/Ethiopian/the_first_epistle_of_clement_to_the_corinthians_87.json, 24 chapters). This book has no KJV/standard-canon counterpart — it is a real 1st-century pastoral letter, almost entirely sustained doctrinal exhortation, so it is structured mostly as role:"law" tiers (Leviticus/Deuteronomy/Pauline-epistle pattern) rather than narrative person tiers. Real textual fact preserved: the letter never names its own author in-body — it speaks corporately as "the Church of God which is at Rome" throughout (1:1); "Clement" is used as a title-only/traditional deliveredBy attribution, same treatment as Hebrews' anonymous authorship in the NT index. The only individually named, book-native characters are the four messengers in the closing (24:3): Claudius, Ephebus, Valerios Bito, Fortunatus. Every other name cited (Cain, Abel, Jacob, Esau, Joseph, Moses, Pharaoh, Aaron, Miriam, Dathan, Abiram, David, Saul, Peter, Paul, Enoch, Noah, Jonah, Abraham, Lot, Rahab, Job, Elias/"Eliaxus", Ezekiel, Judith, Esther, Daniel, Shadrach/Meshach/Abednego, Cephas, Apollos) is a proof-text example only, already indexed under its home book, so these are logged in genealogyLists rather than re-indexed as full characters. Genuine content oddity preserved rather than corrected: 8:18 reads "Elias, and Eliaxus, and Ezekiel" — kept exactly as extracted, not silently normalized to "Elisha." Genuinely distinctive content vs. the standard canon: the Phoenix-of-Arabia resurrection legend (12:2-6, verified against the real source text), offered as literal supporting proof of bodily resurrection — verse 6 is the argument's concluding sentence ("shall we then think it to be any very great and strange thing for the Lord of all to raise up those that religiously serve him...") and is now correctly included in the resurrection_promise_law character's own verse reference alongside verses 2-5, matching the top-level notes' citation.

characters.name: Clement (the Roman Church's voice)

verses.note: letter opens 'THE Church of God which is at Rome, to the Church of God which is at Corinth...grace and peace...be multiplied unto you' — no personal author named.
explains the reply's delay due to 'sudden and unexpected dangers and calamities.'
closes by naming and dispatching the four messengers back to Rome.

funFacts: The title 'Epistle of Clement' is traditional; the body text itself never names an individual author.

characters.name: The Ruin Wrought by Envy
characters.purpose: Diagnoses the Corinthian schism as rooted in envy, proven via a chain of scriptural precedents.

verses.note: 'emulation, and envy, and strife, and sedition, persecution and disorder, war and captivity.'
Cain and Abel, the first case.
Jacob fleeing Esau.
Joseph persecuted; Moses forced to flee Pharaoh.
Aaron and Miriam shut out of the camp seven days.
Dathan and Abiram swallowed by the earth.
David persecuted by Saul.
the martyrdoms of Peter and Paul, by unjust envy.

characters.name: God's Long Patience toward Repentance
characters.purpose: Argues God has always left room for repentance, citing Noah, Jonah, and prophetic calls to turn back.

verses.note: 'Noah preached repentance...Jonah denounced destruction against the Ninevites.'
the Ninevites repented and were saved though strangers to the covenant.
'though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow.'

characters.name: Faith and Hospitality Rewarded
characters.purpose: Sets Enoch, Noah, Abraham, Lot, and Rahab forward as models of faith and hospitality.

verses.note: Enoch, translated, his death unknown.
Noah saved with all living creatures in the ark.
Abraham obeyed God's call and offered Isaac.
Lot saved from Sodom; his wife turned to a pillar of salt.
Rahab hid Joshua's spies and was saved.

characters.name: The Rule of Mercy and Judgment
characters.scribeTier: The Rule of Mercy and Judgment
characters.purpose: Lays down Jesus's reciprocal ethic — mercy for mercy, judgment for judgment — as the community's standard.

verses.note: 'as ye judge, so shall ye be judged...with what measure ye mete, with the same shall it be measured to you again.'
'The merciful shall inherit the earth.'

characters.name: The Humility of Christ Foretold
characters.purpose: Quotes the Suffering Servant oracle in full as the pattern of Christ's humility, stacked with further humble-hearted examples.

verses.note: the Suffering Servant oracle quoted at length.
'Elias, and Eliaxus, and Ezekiel, the prophets' — spelling preserved as extracted.
Abraham calls himself 'dust and ashes.'
Job confesses 'No man is free from pollution.'
Moses at the burning bush: 'Who am I...I am of a slender voice.'
David's penitential psalm quoted at length.

characters.name: The Peace of Creation
characters.purpose: Points to nature's orderly, non-quarreling obedience as a model of peace.

verses.note: the heavens, sun, and moon in orderly concord.
seasons and even the smallest creatures live in peace.

characters.name: The Nearness of God
characters.purpose: Argues from God's omnipresence and full knowledge of thought that the community must choose reverence over factional favor.

verses.note: 'The spirit of the Lord is a candle, searching out the inward parts of the belly.'
'Let us choose to offend a few foolish...men, rather than God.'

characters.name: The Promise of the Resurrection
characters.purpose: Builds a case for bodily resurrection from natural cycles and the legendary Phoenix bird of Arabia.

verses.note: the vine's yearly cycle as a resurrection image.
day/night and sown seed as resurrection images.

the Phoenix of Arabia, reborn every 500 years (vv.2-5), concluding with the argument's point in v.6: 'shall we then think it to be any very great and strange thing for the Lord of all to raise up those that religiously serve him...when even by a bird he shows us the greatness of his power to fulfil his promise?' — distinctive content not in the standard canon.
Job: 'Thou shalt raise up this flesh of mine.'

funFacts: The Phoenix legend is presented as literal supporting evidence for resurrection, a real content difference from the standard 66-book canon.

characters.name: None Can Flee God's Presence
characters.purpose: Warns that no one can outrun God's judgment, then urges holy living.

verses.note: 'If I ascend up into heaven, thou art there...if I shall make my bed in the deep, thy Spirit is there.'
fleeing drunkenness, lust, adultery, and pride.

characters.name: The Blessing of God's Gifts
characters.purpose: Traces the Abrahamic blessing through Isaac, Jacob, the priesthood, kings, and Christ, urging soldier-like orderly obedience.

verses.note: Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob blessed through faith and obedience.
from Jacob came priests, Levites, kings, and Christ 'according to the flesh.'
orderly soldierly obedience as the model for receiving God's gifts.

characters.name: The Order of the Ministry
characters.purpose: Defends the deposed Corinthian ministry's legitimacy as an unbroken chain from Christ through the Apostles, using Aaron's budding rod as precedent.

verses.note: the chief-priest, priests, and Levites each have their proper place.
'The Apostles have preached to us from the Lord Jesus Christ...Christ therefore was sent by God, the Apostles by Christ.'
the budding of Aaron's rod among the twelve tribal rods, as proof God himself settles ministry disputes.
the Apostles appointed successors before their deaths — the letter's core argument against removing the deposed elders.

characters.name: Peace and the Praise of Charity
characters.scribeTier: Peace and the Praise of Charity
characters.purpose: Recalls persecuted-but-faithful examples, invokes Paul's earlier letter to this church over the Cephas/Apollos factions, and closes with a hymn to charity.

verses.note: Daniel; Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego.
invokes Paul's own earlier letter to this church over factions around Paul, Cephas, and Apollos.
the charity hymn: 'Charity unites us to God...our Lord Jesus Christ gave his own blood for us.'

characters.name: Confession and Correction
characters.purpose: Urges the schism's ringleaders to confess or exile themselves for peace, using Moses' intercession at Sinai and Judith and Esther's courage as models, closing with scripture on accepting correction.

verses.note: Moses interceding after the golden calf: 'blot me also out of the book of the living.'
Judith risking herself to deliver Holofernes into a woman's hands.
Esther fasting and humbling herself to deliver the twelve tribes.
'The Lord corrected me, but he did not deliver me over unto death...Happy is the man whom God correct.'

characters.name: Claudius
characters.scribeTier: The Messengers of Peace and Concord

verses.note: named first among the four messengers sent to carry the letter and bring back word from Corinth.

funFacts: Named only in this one closing verse; listed first among the four, which is why he carries the tier.
